id: title:ablaszkiewicz:stop sending frame locals with captured exceptions

review.posthog_relevance: Changes exception reporting behavior in PostHog SDK, potentially reducing credential leakage risk by removing stack trace variables, though this also removes the ability to opt-in to sending these variables.
review.reason: P1.F1.H2 removes a conditional and an import, changing exception reporting behavior to unconditionally disable sending stack trace variables. P1.F1.H1 is a minor cleanup. The tier is assigned based on the substantive behavior change in P1.F1.H2.
review.uncertainty: The actual impact on credential leakage and the trade-off between security and opt-in capability are not independently verified; this relies on the supplied observations and comments.

observations.limitations: Only P1.F1.H2 contains substantive behavioral changes; P1.F1.H1 is a removal of an unused import. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Removes unused import, no runtime behavior change.
observations.posthog_connection: Removes dependency on a utility no longer used in the ready() lifecycle.

observations.behavior: Replaces conditional exception variable capture with unconditional False, removing the str_to_bool dependency.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes exception reporting behavior: the PostHog SDK will no longer send exception stack trace variables, regardless of the TEMPORAL_DISABLE_EXCEPTION_VARIABLE_CAPTURE setting. This could reduce credential leakage risk if frame locals are not reliably redacted, but also removes the ability to opt-in to sending these variables. observations.behavior: Adds comment explaining the rationale for the unconditional False setting.
observations.code_quote: # Frame locals can hold credentials that the SDK masking does not reliably redact, so never send them.
observations.posthog_connection: Documents the security rationale for the behavior change.
